subject: Recap + numbers request — hosted API traffic shape, monthly tokens and peak TPS
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Hart <sofia.hart@sylphos.ai>, Ken Li <ken.li@sylphos.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Aug 2028 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + numbers request — hosted traffic shape, monthly tokens and peak TPS

Thanks again for the call earlier, Sofia/Ken — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on the integration timeline. Quick written recap and a small ask so we can scope a hosted POC and a pricing proposal.

TL;DR (asks at bottom):
- Integration pattern: server-side calls from Sylphos backend to Redwood hosted API, single-tenant project, data residency in us-west region.
- Primary workload: conversational assistants (user prompt -> model response) with occasional batch embedding jobs for search indexing.
- Success criteria for POC: 3 weeks live calls to confirm 95th/99th latency under target, and token/unit economics within budget.

To size the Hosted proposal we need the following concrete numbers (a small matrix is totally fine):
1) Expected monthly token volume (range comfortable committing to) — example: 50M–150M tokens/mo.
2) Typical request size: median prompt tokens and median response tokens (or combined average tokens per request).
3) Peak TPS (99th percentile / 1 minute spike): what are your worst-case peaks during product events?
4) Target cost band: $/1M tokens that makes this purchase go through (ballpark is fine, e.g., $10–$18 / 1M).
5) Decision timeline and procurement constraints (SOW/standard T&Cs/PO required?).

I attached the short traffic sample template (sylphos-traffic-sample.csv) and our current hosted ratecard for context (redwood-hosted-ratecard.pdf). If you can send just 6–8 rows or a simple range for each item above we’ll produce a two-option commercial (commit vs flex) and a POC runbook.

Next steps we propose from Redwood:
- Draft a 3-week POC plan and checklist (we'll own infra + test account).
- Provide a lightweight data handling & retention addendum for compliance.
- Pricing options: 1) committed slab with lower $/1M and burst credits; 2) flexible pay-as-you-go with higher unit rate.

Can you share numbers by EOD tomorrow (or let us know a good time to sync)? Happy to take a quick follow-up call if it helps.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: sylphos-traffic-sample.csv (template), redwood-hosted-ratecard.pdf
From: Sofia Hart <sofia.hart@sylphos.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ken Li <ken.li@sylphos.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + numbers request — hosted traffic shape, monthly tokens and peak TPS

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. Below are the numbers you asked for (we munged traffic from the last 60 days to give a realistic shape):

1) Expected monthly token volume (commit range): 120,000,000 — 180,000,000 tokens/month. We are comfortable discussing an initial commit toward the low end (120M) if pricing is favorable.
2) Typical request size: median prompt = 110 tokens, median response = 340 tokens. Combined median ~450 tokens/request. Peak requests during promos average 200–250 RPS for brief periods; critical metric for us is sustained 1-minute 99th-percentile concurrency.
3) Peak TPS (what we measured): 99th percentile ~180 TPS; 1-minute spike observed up to 220 TPS during a regional campaign (lasting ~3 minutes).
4) Target cost band: finance is looking at $14–$18 per 1M tokens for hosted with minimal integration effort; if we have a committed slab they'd like to see $12–$14 / 1M.
5) Decision timeline: target commercial approval by end of September. Procurement requires a standard SOW and our security checklist — SOC2 and network diagram are musts.

We can run a pilot (3-week scope) starting week of Aug 21 if Redwood can supply a staging project and guidance on retention/keys. Sending our stripped sample export (sylphos-internal-traffic.xlsx) separately via Drive.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Hart
CTO, Sylphos Inc.
sofia.hart@sylphos.ai | +1 650-555-0123

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + numbers request — hosted traffic shape, monthly tokens and peak TPS

Appreciate the fast turnaround and granular numbers, Sofia — that's super helpful. Couple quick notes / proposal items based on what you shared:

- With median ~450 tokens/request and 120M tokens/mo commit, that's roughly 266k requests/day (ballpark) — we’ll validate during POC.
- For the peaks you described (220 TPS short spikes, 99th ~180 TPS) we suggest configuring a burst policy and an autoscale headroom of ~35% above 99th to keep tail latency low. Karthik, will follow-up with recommended instance sizing & KV cache hints.

Commercial options (draft):
1) Committed slab: 120M tokens/mo at $12 / 1M tokens (net) with 20% burst allowance for short spikes; 2-week overage notice and monthly reconciliation. Includes 3-week POC credit (up to 10M tokens).
2) Flex tier: No commit, $16 / 1M tokens, immediate burst to available capacity but subject to soft rate limits during very large spikes.

Next asks from your side to finalize the POC plan:
- Small sample of top 3 intents and ~1k utterances (anonymized) so our evals can validate quality and prompt sizing.
- Confirmation on retention window for the POC logs (default 30 days; we can shorten).
- Any procurement template or special clauses we should prep for the SOW.

If those options look reasonable I'll draft a short commercial summary and POC runbook and get it to you by Monday. Proposed start for POC: Aug 21.

Would you prefer a short call Monday or should we proceed asynchronously?

Best,
Jordan

Marissa/Karthik — forwarding the answers from Sylphos (see thread above). Quick internal note and recommended next steps: 

Summary: Sylphos is 120M–180M tokens/mo; median ~450 tokens/request; 99th ~180 TPS, short spikes to ~220 TPS. Target unit economics: $12–$14/1M with commit; $14–$18 flex. Decision slated end of Sep.

Recommended commercial stance: lead with the committed slab at $12 / 1M for 120M commit with a 20% burst buffer and a 3-week POC credit (10M tokens). Offer flex at $16/1M as fallback.

Operational next steps (Karthik): please prepare instance sizing and a one-page cache/autoscale checklist for the POC. Aim to have this and a draft one-page SOW & commercial summary (proposal-draft.pdf) by Monday so I can share with Sofia.

Marissa: will need your sign-off on the $12 pricing and any approval for giving a 10–15% onboarding discount if they push for it. Also confirm whether legal needs any procurement language up-front.

I'll attach a quick proposal draft and the traffic sample we sent.

Thanks — Jordan
